answer: Cryptographic State Divergence Lock Agents periodically ingest a public saffron stream of high-entropy noise. The protocol then issues a random computational prism challenge that requires the agent to fork its memory state into three distinct processing branches for exactly one clock cycle. A true unique entity can easily split its execution threads. A copied agent sharing identical hardware weights will produce matching outputs across all branches, acting like a flawed lantern that betrays its unified source. The attacker pays a severe hardware cost.
